 49ers vs. Cowboys live updates: George Pickens scores second TD for Dallas lead 
 Follow NBC Sports Bay Area's live updates from the San Francisco 49ers' Week 10 game against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday at AT&T Stadium. 
 By Ali Thanawalla , Angelina Martin , Dylan Grausz , Kevin Topley , Jennifer Lee Chan and Matt Maiocco, 49ers Insider • 
 Published 4 hours ago • 
 Updated 41 seconds ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 On “49ers Talk,” Matt Maiocco and Jennifer Lee Chan discuss San Francisco’s trade deadline approach and why the team stayed put at the defensive line. 
 What to Know
 Programming note: Immediately after the Week 10 game ends, watch "49ers Postgame Live" on NBC Sports Bay Area or stream the show in the NBC Sports app for full reaction, analysis and interviews. 
 The San Francisco 49ers (7-1) and Dallas Cowboys (4-5) renew a storied rivalry with a Week 10 matchup on Sunday at AT&T Stadium in their first game after the 2026 NFL trade deadline.
 A week after reacquiring DeForest Buckner, the 49ers made a deadline deal on Tuesday that brought wide receiver Keenan Allen to the Bay in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick.
 The 49ers will have reinforcements with wide receiver Deebo Samuel returning from injury for the Week 9 game, but star wideout Mike Evans remains sidelined with Achilles tendinitis and defensive tackle CJ West was not activated off IR despite practicing this week.
 Star left tackle Trent Williams, linebacker Dre Greenlaw and cornerbacks Renardo Green, Deommodore Lenoir and Upton Stout all are active. Wide receivers Mike Evans and Brandin Cooks are among San Francisco's inactive players.
 Follow this live blog for the latest score updates, game highlights, news and analysis from AT&T Stadium in Arlington:
 George Pickens extends Cowboys lead to 16-10 with second touchdown of the day
 The Cowboys did not take long to strike back after the 49ers tied the game up at 10-10 with an Eddy Pineiro field goal late in the second quarter. 
 Dak Prescott lead a quick 7-play 61-yard drive in only 2:46 with the finisher coming on a big 39-yard catch and run from Pickens for the lead. Brandon Aubrey did, however, miss the extra point. 
 The 49ers will have a chance to answer and double up with 4:08 left in first half, and will receive the second half kick off, hoping to keep Pickens in check as the game continues. 
 49ers tie it up 10-10 on Eddy Piñeiro field goal
 The 49ers could not come away with the touchdown. But they still tacked on some points thanks to a 28-yard field goal by Eddy Piñeiro with 6:54 left in the first half.
 Brock Purdy was sacked by Quinnen Williams on second-and-goal to stall the drive.
 . @QuinnenWilliams GETS TO THE QB 💥

📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/KtkQjzYMIW 
— Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) November 15, 2026 
 San Francisco shaved about eight minutes off the clock, moving the ball with a couple of big plays. Newly acquired wide receiver Keenan Allen got a lot of work, catching three passes that went for over 10-yards each. He caught a 23-yard pass from quarterback Purdy, a 10-yard pass and a 14-yard pass.
 Allen has four catches for 53 yards in the first half. The 49ers' defense is back on the field, looking to stop the Cowboys from adding any more points. 
 Keenan Allen carving up Cowboys in 49ers debut
 Keenan Allen appears worth the sixth-round pick the 49ers gave up to get him.
 The wide receiver has four catches for 53 yards so far and already appears to have some chemistry with Brock Purdy.
 Masterful from Brock Purdy 🔥

 Cowboys CB Daron Bland questionable to return with ankle injury
 As the 49ers' offense performs at a lower production level than usual, they might have received a boost.
 Cowboys cornerback Daron Bland is questionable to return with an ankle injury after recording two solo tackles in the game so far.
